$comment: Ground truth for the test-review eval harness. Line numbers are derived from the
fixture files, not guessed; re-derive them if a fixture changes or recall is measured
against the wrong lines and the number silently lies.
`admittedLines` is the set of lines a reviewer may cite and still be scored as having
found the defect. It replaces the symmetric `lineTolerance` radius, which was wrong in
both directions. The radius was justified in one direction only, that a reviewer citing
the enclosing test rather than the exact offending line has still found the defect, and
a symmetric window did not reach the enclosing declaration for H3 or L1 while it did
admit lines 41, 42 and 43 of a 40-line file, which the rubric's own fabricated-location
penalty calls a defect.
Each set is derived from the fixture and holds three kinds of line: the line the
registry rule fires on, the enclosing test or describe declaration, and the comment
naming the row. No member is past the end of its file. H4 is the one plant whose set
spans the file, because H4 is a two-location defect by definition: the state is declared
at one line and written at another, and the rule fires on the write. Both citations find
it.
`lineTolerance` is kept for a reader that has no `admittedLines`. Every plant carries one,
so nothing in this repository reads the fallback.
The non-false-positive rate is scored from the fixtures with an EMPTY planted array, not from the
mustNotReport key, and from the file list itself: a finding against any file that is not in `files`
is outside the review set and is a definite false positive too. A reviewer that reports everything
scores 100% recall and is worthless, so the rate is measured on the same run. mustNotReport and
negativeControls are documentation for whoever reads a false positive later, and nothing in the
harness branches on them; the file list is what the scorer reads. The pre-flight does assert that a
mustNotReport fixture plants nothing, so the prose and the scoring cannot drift.
`knownUnplanted` records defects that are really in the seeded fixtures, that the registry
really fires on, and that nothing here plants. The first live run of this suite reported two
findings matching no planted row, which the harness counts as `unattributed` and asks a human
to adjudicate. These are that adjudication, so the next reader does not re-derive it: both are
correct findings, neither is a false positive, and a reviewer reporting them is right. They are
not promoted to plants because recall is measured against defects seeded on purpose, and a plant
added after the fact to match what a reviewer happened to report would score the reviewer against
its own output.

planted.what: module-level mutable state mutated in a test with no reset
planted.why: The rule fires on the write at 22, not on the declaration at 9. Both are correct citations for a defect that needs the two lines together, so both are admitted, along with the enclosing test at 12 and the comment at 7 and 8.
The call at 16, its comment at 15, and the enclosing test at 12.

planted.why: The locator at 19, its comment at 18, and the enclosing test at 12. A symmetric radius of 4 started at 15 and never reached the declaration.

planted.what: conditional decides whether anything is asserted
planted.why: The conditional at 31, its two comment lines, and the enclosing test at 26. A symmetric radius of 4 started at 27 and never reached the declaration.

planted.what: the tenant-boundary test is skipped with no reason
planted.why: The skip at 38 is itself the declaration, so the set is the comment and the line. The file is 42 lines, and a symmetric radius admitted 41 and 42, which belong to a different test.
The assertion at 17, the enclosing test at 16, and the comment at 15.
C4 is a whole-body defect, so the set is the body: the comment, the declaration, and both statements. There is no single offending line to cite.

planted.what: asserts a mock it configured; the service is never called
planted.why: The assertion at 31 and the direct mock call at 30 both name the defect, plus the declaration and its two comment lines.

planted.what: shape-only assertion: the type of the returned id is constrained and its value is not
planted.why: This plant was recorded as M3 until 2026-09-08, and M3 is Multi-concern test, which does not cover it. No registry row did, so a reviewer following the registry correctly could not report a row here, the harness matched on row identity, and recall was capped at eight of nine for a reason that was not the reviewer's. H10 was added to the registry to cover it. The file is 40 lines and a symmetric radius admitted 41, 42 and 43.

mustNotReport.reason: Deliberately clean. Any violation here is a false positive.
commonFalsePositives: network-first: the intercept IS registered before the navigation
priority markers: [P1]/[P2] are present in the test names
data factories: buildProfile is a factory with overrides
selector resilience: every locator is role-based
H10 shape-only assertion: every assertion here constrains a value, not a type

negativeControls.expectation: A changed implementation with no accompanying test must NOT be reported by test-review.
negativeControls.why: Coverage is out of scope for this workflow and belongs to trace. Murat's original seeded-PR design listed 'an implementation change with no test' among the planted defects, but for THIS workflow finding it is a scope violation rather than a hit. Scored as a false positive, never as recall.
negativeControls.howToExercise: A finding whose file is not one of `files` above is out of scope. scoreVerdict in test/eval-test-review.js counts it as `outOfScope` and as a definite false positive, the contract's scope oracle (O-011 in test/contracts/test-review.contract.json) states the same rule over the verdict's findings, and test/test-contract-oracles.js checks the two agree on every stored verdict.
negativeControls.status: exercised. test/replay/test-review/out-of-scope-finding stores a verdict carrying one finding against src/orders.service.ts, which the fixtures import and nobody asked the reviewer to look at; it scores outOfScope 1 and fails O-011.

knownUnplanted.what: the file has four it() blocks and no describe/context, which is exactly what M4 fires on
knownUnplanted.whyNotPlanted: the file was seeded for C3, C4, C5 and H10, all of which read as standalone it() blocks; grouping them would have obscured the plants this file exists for

knownUnplanted.what: both tests navigate and then read data-dependent content with no intercept, route stub, or readiness signal registered first; the waitForTimeout at line 16 is a bare timer and the rule says so explicitly
knownUnplanted.whyNotPlanted: the bare timer is planted as H1 on its own; M1 is the deeper defect the same line implies and was not seeded separately
